title: Convex radius bonus in the hop objective
spec: Give _solve_once an optional argument gamma (default 0). The SLSQP objective becomes -(sum(r) + gamma * sum(r**2)). In the basin-hopping loop, call it with gamma = rng.uniform(-2, 2) on half of the steps and gamma = 0 on the others. Positive gamma favours unequal radii, negative gamma favours equal radii, so the solver is pushed towards different size distributions and contact graphs. Candidates are still scored and accepted by the plain repaired sum of radii. When a candidate from a step with gamma != 0 comes within 0.002 of the incumbent sum, run one more _solve_once from it with gamma = 0 before the acceptance test, so that it is compared at a true local optimum.

title: Heavy-tailed initial radii
spec: In _solve_once, when x0 is None, replace the constant INIT_RADIUS starting radii with a log-normal draw: r0 = INIT_RADIUS * exp(rng.normal(0, 0.5, n)), clipped to [0.005, 0.2]. This gives the first SLSQP run a spread of sizes instead of uniform circles, which may seed a more varied basin before basin hopping starts. Centres stay uniform in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Only the initial radii change.

title: Multi-candidate relocation with real solves screening
spec: At each basin-hopping step generate 3 perturbed starts (each with the smallest-circle relocation), run SLSQP with maxiter=25 on each, and fully continue (maxiter 200) only the one with the highest partial radius sum after repair-free evaluation (sum of radii minus total overlap violation). Accept as before.

title: Proximal anchor penalty in basin hopping
spec: In basin-hopping solves, add to the SLSQP objective a small term 1e-3 * sum((v - x0)**2) over centres only, with its gradient, so the solve stays near the perturbed start and explores local basins; for the final 20 percent of time set the coefficient to 0. Everything else is unchanged.

title: Radius-reset kick
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.3 per step, replace the perturbed radii r0 with 0.7 * br (the incumbent radii scaled down uniformly) instead of br plus Gaussian noise. Centres still get the usual N(0, 0.02) noise and the _relocate call. This gives SLSQP room to rearrange the contacts before the circles regrow. All other steps (the usual radius noise) stay unchanged.

title: Smooth shear-field collective kick
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, on half of the steps (chosen with rng) replace the independent Gaussian centre noise with a smooth low-frequency displacement field. Draw amplitudes A, B ~ N(0, 0.03), integer wave numbers kx, ky in {1, 2} and phases in [0, 2*pi) with rng. Set dx = A * sin(2*pi*ky*y + phase1) and dy = B * sin(2*pi*kx*x + phase2), computed from the incumbent centres, add them to the centres and clip to [0, 1]. Neighbouring circles then move together, rows and columns slide past each other, and the contact graph changes along a line instead of everywhere. On these steps add radius noise of sd 0.005 only. _relocate, SLSQP, _repair and acceptance run as before.

title: Cheap hops with a full re-solve only on improvement
spec: Add a parameter maxiter to _solve_once (default MAX_ITER). In the basin-hopping loop use maxiter=80 for each candidate solve. If the repaired candidate sum is within 0.002 of the incumbent or better, re-run _solve_once from the candidate's centres and radii with maxiter=400, repair, and compare that result with the incumbent instead. This gives more hops per second while still converging the promising ones fully.

title: Contact-graph-guided perturbation
spec: After each accepted incumbent, compute contacts (pairs with gap < 1e-6). Perturb with noise scaled per circle: sd 0.04 for circles with fewer than 3 contacts (rattlers or loose ones) and sd 0.01 for circles with 3 or more contacts. Everything else in the loop is unchanged.

title: Log-uniform random perturbation size per step
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, draw sigma = exp(rng.uniform(log(0.005), log(0.05))) once per step and use it for both the centre noise and the radius noise in place of the fixed 0.02. Steps then mix fine local refinements with larger escapes, with no schedule to tune. Everything else stays the same.

title: Squared-distance pair constraints in SLSQP
spec: In _solve_once, replace the pair constraint sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) - r_i - r_j >= 0 with the squared form dx^2+dy^2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 >= 0, and additionally require r_i+r_j >= 0 implicitly through the bounds already in place. The squared form removes the square-root singularity at zero distance, giving smoother gradients for SLSQP. Keep the same pair index arrays, the same wall constraints, and the same MAX_ITER. Only the cons function changes, so the rest of the basin-hopping loop stays identical.

title: Elite pool crossover
spec: Keep a pool of the 5 best distinct packings (distinct by sum differing by >1e-5). With probability 0.2 per step, build a child by choosing a random vertical or horizontal line at coordinate u~U(0.3,0.7), taking circles from the best packing on one side and from a different pool member on the other side, then fixing the count to n by dropping the smallest overlaps or adding relocated smallest circles. Solve with SLSQP from this child, repair, and insert into the pool.

title: Keep an elite pair of packings and restart from the worse one
spec: Maintain two packings: the incumbent and a second elite packing that is the best of all candidates whose radius sum is within 0.003 of the incumbent but differs from it in centre layout. Each basin-hopping step picks its parent at random from the two elites, with probability 0.5 each. Update the elites with each new candidate. This keeps a small population of distinct good basins instead of a single chain, and it uses only the existing moves, with no new solver code.

title: Tighter SLSQP ftol in every basin-hopping solve
spec: In _solve_once add 'ftol': 1e-10 to the SLSQP options dict (keep maxiter=MAX_ITER). SciPy's default ftol of 1e-6 can stop the solve before contacts are fully tight, and the repair step then loses some radius. This is a one-line change with no other edits.

title: Greedy radius inflation after repair
spec: After _repair produces a valid packing, add a pass that inflates each radius to its maximum feasible value given all other circles fixed. Loop over circles in order of increasing radius, and for each circle set r_i to min(wall distance, min over j of (d_ij - r_j)). Repeat the sweep twice. This recovers slack that the max-overlap repair leaves behind, and it is O(n^2) per sweep, which is cheap at n=32. Output must stay valid under the 1e-10 tolerance, so subtract a 1e-12 margin in the final radii.

title: Deflated feasible start for each hop
spec: In the basin-hopping loop of solve, replace the radius perturbation r0 = max(br + N(0, 0.02), 0) with a deterministic deflation r0 = 0.85 * br (new constant DEFLATE = 0.85). Keep the centre noise of sd 0.02 and the _relocate call as they are. The aim is that SLSQP starts from a nearly feasible point with slack around every circle, so it can rearrange and regrow, instead of starting from random overlaps of about 0.02 that force large first steps. Nothing else changes.

title: Feasibility-shrunk start before SLSQP
spec: Before each SLSQP call in basin hopping, shrink the candidate radii so that the starting point is roughly feasible: multiply r0 by 0.9 and then cap each radius by its wall distance. SLSQP then starts from a nearly valid packing, which usually keeps the iterates on the feasible side and reduces the number of pair constraints it violates early. The shrink factor is the only new constant. Nothing else in the loop changes.

title: Adaptive SLSQP iteration cap
spec: Use MAX_ITER=60 for basin-hopping solves (warm-started from a perturbed incumbent, they usually converge quickly) and keep 200 for the first solve. Gives more hops per 24 s. Optionally if the 60-iteration result has a sum within 0.01 of the incumbent, re-run it with the remaining 140 iterations warm-started from the result.

title: Swap small and large circle move
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.3 before the SLSQP solve, pick one circle among the 5 smallest radii and one among the 5 largest, swap their centres (keeping radii attached to the circles, then shrink the swapped radii to fit, e.g. set both to the mean radius), then proceed with the existing perturbation, relocation and solve. Accept via the existing rule.

title: Relocate the two smallest circles per hop
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, call _relocate twice in a row with probability 0.5 (using rng), and once otherwise. After the first call the moved circle usually has a larger radius, so the second call moves the next smallest circle. This allows moves that need two small circles shifted at once, which single relocation followed by greedy acceptance cannot reach. Add the constant DOUBLE_PROB = 0.5. _relocate itself, the noise and the acceptance rule do not change.

title: Tight-tolerance final polish of the incumbent
spec: Keep the search loop as it is, but reserve the last 10 percent of the TIME_FRACTION budget for one final polish of the best packing only. Run SLSQP on the incumbent centres and radii with ftol=1e-12 and maxiter=500, using the same constraints as _solve_once. Pass the result through _repair and keep it only if its radius sum beats the incumbent. This targets the small convergence gap left by the default SLSQP ftol of 1e-6 without spending time on the search itself.

title: Squared-distance pair constraints
spec: In _solve_once, change the pair non-overlap constraint from sqrt(dist^2) - r_i - r_j >= 0 to the smooth form dist^2 - (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0, where dist^2 = ((c_i - c_j)**2).sum(1). This removes the sqrt, whose gradient is badly behaved when centres nearly coincide after the relocation and noise step, and gives SLSQP's finite differences a polynomial constraint. Leave the wall and r >= 0 constraints as they are. Leave _repair unchanged, since it still checks true distances and keeps the packing valid. Nothing else changes.

title: Half-square reflection kick
spec: Add a topology move to the basin-hopping loop. With probability 0.15 per step (constant REFLECT_PROB), before the Gaussian noise, pick an axis a in {0, 1} and a side at random with rng. For every incumbent circle whose centre coordinate a lies on that side of 0.5, reflect that coordinate within the half: x -> 0.5 - x for the lower half, x -> 1.5 - x for the upper half. Radii are kept. Circles that straddle the midline may now overlap; the usual noise, _relocate, SLSQP and _repair deal with that. Acceptance is unchanged (the candidate must beat the incumbent). The aim is to recombine a good half-packing with a mirrored interface, a large coherent move that Gaussian noise cannot make.

title: Clip perturbed centres to stay inside the walls
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, after adding noise, clip each centre to [r0_i, 1 - r0_i] (using the perturbed, non-negative radius, capped at 0.5) instead of to [0, 1]. Do the same in _relocate, which already picks feasible radii. This gives SLSQP starting points that never violate a wall constraint. Apply the clip after the radius noise is computed and before _relocate. No other change.

title: Delaunay hole candidates for relocation
spec: In _relocate, replace the 30 uniform random candidate points with the actual holes of the current packing. Compute scipy.spatial.Delaunay on the centres of all circles except k, plus the four square corners and four edge midpoints as extra points. Take the circumcentre of every triangle, keep those inside [0, 1]^2, and add 10 uniform random points as a fallback. For each candidate p compute rk = max(min(p.min(), (1 - p).min(), (d - r).min()), 0) with the k-th circle excluded, vectorised over candidates. Choose a candidate at random among the 3 with the largest rk, using rng, so that successive hops differ. Set c[k], r[k] to that point and its rk. Wrap the Delaunay call in try/except and fall back to the existing random-trial code on any error. The function signature stays the same.

title: Halton start with random scramble
spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres in the first _solve_once by a Halton sequence in bases 2 and 3 with a random Cranley-Patterson shift (add rng.uniform(size=2) mod 1), scaled to [0.05,0.95]. Keep INIT_RADIUS. Only the first start is affected.

title: Relocate the two smallest circles
spec: Change _relocate to take a parameter m (default 1) and relocate the m smallest circles one after another. Each one is moved to the best of `trials` random points by the existing local score, and the score uses the radii already updated in that call. In the basin-hopping loop call it with m = 2 with probability 0.5, otherwise m = 1. No other changes.

title: Final tight-tolerance SLSQP polish of the incumbent
spec: After the basin-hopping loop ends (at TIME_FRACTION of the budget), run one more SLSQP solve starting from the best (centres, radii). Use options={'maxiter': 1000, 'ftol': 1e-12} through a new optional parameter of _solve_once (default stays as now). Clip the centres to [0,1], repair, and keep the result only if its repaired sum of radii beats the incumbent. Check the clock inside the polish: if less than 3 s remains before time_limit, skip it. Nothing else changes.

title: Radius-proportional centre noise
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, replace the centre perturbation rng.normal(0, 0.02, bc.shape) with rng.normal(0, 1, bc.shape) * (0.4 * br[:, None] + 0.005), so that each circle's displacement scales with its radius (for a typical r ~0.09 this is about 0.04, for small circles about 0.01). Radius noise and relocation stay unchanged.

title: Inverse-radius-weighted relocation target
spec: In _relocate, pick the circle to move at random with probability proportional to 1 / (r_i + 0.01)^2, using the seeded rng, instead of always argmin(r). The same small circle then is not moved every step, and other near-rattlers also get tried. The trials and the scoring stay unchanged.

title: Small random affine kick
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.3 per step, apply a random affine map about (0.5, 0.5) to the incumbent centres instead of the per-circle Gaussian noise: c0 = 0.5 + (bc - 0.5) @ (I + A).T, where A has i.i.d. N(0, 0.03) entries. Then clip to [0,1] and add N(0, 0.005) per-centre noise. Radii get the usual noise, and _relocate is still applied. This is a collective shear or stretch that can move many contacts at once.

title: Alternating perturbation axis
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, alternate between two kinds of kick on successive steps. On even steps perturb only the centres (radii copied from the incumbent). On odd steps perturb only the radii (centres copied from the incumbent, with noise sd 0.02 applied to radii only). Keep _relocate and the acceptance rule unchanged. The goal is to separate topology moves from size moves so each is less likely to be undone by the other.

title: Radius-proportional perturbation noise
spec: In the basin-hopping step, scale the centre noise for each circle by its own radius: c0 = bc + rng.normal(0, sigma * (br / br.mean())[:, None], bc.shape), keeping sigma = 0.02. Large circles then move less and small circles move more, which matches the rattler-heavy structure of good packings. Radii noise stays the same. Clipping to [0, 1] and _relocate are unchanged.

title: Final tight-tolerance SLSQP polish of the incumbent
spec: After the basin-hopping loop ends at TIME_FRACTION of the time, run one extra SLSQP solve from the unperturbed incumbent (x0 = concatenate([bc.ravel(), br])) with options maxiter=300 and ftol=1e-12. To do this, give _solve_once optional maxiter and ftol arguments and pass them into the options dict; the in-loop calls keep the defaults. Clip the centres, apply _repair, and replace the incumbent only if the repaired sum is larger. Before starting, check that at least 4 s of CPU time remain (time.process_time() - t0 < time_limit - 4); skip the polish otherwise. The aim is to recover the roughly 1e-6 to 1e-4 slack left by the default ftol and the proportional shrinking in _repair.

title: Scale-aware relocation neighbourhood
spec: In _relocate, the neighbour cutoff is currently the fixed value 0.05 added to rk + r. Replace it with a cutoff proportional to the typical circle size, nb = d < rk + r + 1.5 * np.mean(r). Circles with big radii then count as neighbours over a wider distance, so the relocation score reflects the local crowding more accurately. The scoring formula and the number of trials stay the same.

title: Native box bounds for SLSQP
spec: In _solve_once, remove the four wall blocks (c-r, 1-c-r) and the r>=0 block from cons and instead pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Keep only the pair-distance constraints in cons plus wall constraints c-r>=0 and 1-c-r>=0 (these are still needed, so keep them), but drop the redundant r>=0 block by using bounds on r. This shrinks the constraint vector and speeds each SLSQP solve, allowing more basin-hopping steps in the time budget.

title: Log-uniform random sigma per basin-hopping step
spec: Replace the fixed centre-noise sd of 0.02 in the basin-hopping step with a fresh value drawn each step: sigma = exp(rng.uniform(log(0.003), log(0.05))). Use this sigma for both the centre and the radius noise on that step. Spreading the step size over a log range gives the chain both fine local moves and coarse jumps without any schedule to tune. The relocation step and acceptance rule are unchanged.

title: Forced-size insertion with neighbour deflation
spec: Extend _relocate with a parameter force (default False). When force is True, after the best point p is chosen, set the moved circle's radius to the median of r instead of the hole radius rk, capped by the distance from p to the nearest wall. Then, for every other circle j that now overlaps it, set r[j] = max(d_j - r[k], 0.2 * r[j]), where d_j is the centre distance. The small circle is thus planted as a full-size circle and its neighbours give way. Plain relocation leaves it as a small circle in a hole, and SLSQP then tends to push it straight back. In the loop, call _relocate with force=True with probability 0.3 (constant FORCE_PROB), chosen with rng. SLSQP, _repair and greedy acceptance are unchanged.

title: Final LP polish of radii
spec: After the basin-hopping loop, take the best centres and solve a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog (highs): maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, r_i <= wall distance of centre i, r_i >= 0, with centres fixed. Subtract SHRINK 1e-9 from the result, run the existing _repair for safety, and return it only if its sum beats the current best. Also apply this LP in place of _repair inside the loop for candidate evaluation.

title: One-fifth-rule perturbation sigma
spec: Replace the fixed 0.02 noise sd in basin hopping with an adaptive sigma starting at 0.02. After each step multiply sigma by 1.2 if the candidate improved the incumbent, otherwise by 1.2**(-0.25). Clip sigma to [0.003, 0.08]. Use sigma for both centre and radius noise.
